A weak line of convergence associated with a broad trough centered
near Yap State and easterly trade winds is sitting over the Marianas
and bringing scattered showers to the region through tomorrow with
isolated thunderstorms. The risk for isolated thunderstorms will
continue through at least Sunday night as an upper-level trough
moves into the region and wind shear increases significantly.
However, a diffusive low-level flow and dry upper level air will 
likely keep storm coverage isolated. By Monday, the upper level
trough will start to move out and only isolated showers are 
anticipated the rest of the forecast period. As winds decrease over
the next couple of days, there is a slight chance for island-effect 
showers Tuesday and Wednesday over Guam.

Marine...
Gentle to moderate easterlies will prevail across the Marianas
through the weekend, then begin to lighten as a broad trough 
extending in eastern Yap State continues to bring patchy showers 
and isolated thunderstorms through Sunday. Increased upper-level
instability late Sunday through Monday morning may allow for
further isolated thunderstorm development. Combined seas of 6 to 8 
feet will persist through tonight and then begin to slowly taper down
thereafter, as the east-northeasterly swell and westerly swell start
to diminish. This is also contributing to a moderate risk of rip 
currents along west, north, and east-facing reefs. There is also a 
moderate risk of lightning for the coastlines through at least Sunday
night.

Tropical Systems...
30W was upgraded to Tropical Storm In-fa over the northern Marshall
Islands at 700 AM ChST this morning, and is currently located near 
10.4N 166.2E, or 110 miles north-northeast of Ujae Atoll, south of 
Bikini and Rongelap Atolls. Himawari visible satellite imagery this 
afternoon shows increasingly organized convective bands wrapping 
into the center, with heavy showers and thunderstorms mainly focused 
along In-fa's western flanks and around the center, covering Ujae, 
Bikini, and Rongelap Atolls, and northern portions of Kwajalein 
Atoll. Scatterometry data from this morning shows strong to near-gale
sustained west to southwest winds across Ujae Atoll and south of the
center, and fresh to strong winds extending farther south and 
southeast, across Kwajalein to around Ailinglaplap. Currently, In-fa 
has maximum sustained winds of 50 mph, extending outward from the 
center up to 90 miles.

In-fa remains nearly stationary, with its recent motion showing a 
slight south-southwest drift at around 2 mph, but it is forecast to 
begin slowly meandering north-northwest through tonight. Then, In-fa
will see a slight increase in forward speed Sunday as it begins to 
exit the Marshall Islands. Currently, there are no Tropical Storm 
Watches or Warnings in effect across the region, but this may change 
if In-fa develops more rapidly than the current forecast indicates, 
or is slower to move out of the RMI than expected. In-fa is forecast
to intensify through Sunday, possibly becoming a strong tropical 
storm by this evening, and then potentially strengthen into a 
Category 1 typhoon early Sunday morning.

For more information on Tropical Storm In-fa, please refer to 
bulletins from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header 
WTPN31 PGTW and from the National Weather Service under WMO header 
WTPQ31 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
Himawari visible satellite this afternoon shows a strengthening,
nearly-stationary Tropical Storm In-fa positioned over the northern
Marshall Islands, discussed above. Pohnpei and Kosrae sit just south
of the stronger westerly inflow and associated showers, but swaths 
of upper-level debris clouds are drifting over both islands this 
afternoon, from prior convection to the north. Models depict an 
increase in showers near Pohnpei late overnight through Sunday as 
In-fa's inflow bands, and associated low-level convergence, move 
into the area, while Kosrae remains just farther south. For Majuro, a
surface ridging pattern will dominate over the coming days as In-fa
slowly lifts out of the Marshall Islands, and showers are expected to
remain isolated there for much of the forecast period. Winds will 
remain light to moderate at all three locations through the coming 
week, largely influenced by the position of TS In-fa, with winds 
shifting from northwest to west for Pohnpei, west to southwest for 
Kosrae, and remaining out of the southwest for Majuro through the 
remainder of the weekend and early next week.

Generally benign marine conditions are expected at Pohnpei, Kosrae,
and Majuro, with combined seas around 4 to 7 feet, comprised of a 
primary swell out of the north to northeast, and a secondary 
southeast swell. Seas look to increase by a foot or two for Majuro
through Sunday night as west to southwest swell builds into the 
area, then subside early next week. Seas will be hazardous to small
